record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.context_brief: existence of a 2DPDA member in a family
record.original_question: Given a family of languages of the kind constructed in the paper, does at least one language in that family belong to 2DPDA, the class of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages?

evidence.quote: (2) Does one of a given family of languages belong to 2DPDA ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-way deterministic pushdown automaton (2DPDA) is a deterministic machine equipped with a finite-state control, a read-only input tape (with endmarkers) on which the input head may move left, right, or stay, and a pushdown store on which the machine may push or pop a single symbol per step. The class 2DPDA is the class of languages accepted by such machines.

Consider the following construction. For each natural number n, let L_n be a language over a fixed alphabet, defined so that the family { L_n : n ≥ 1 } encodes, in a uniform way, computations of arbitrary deterministic Turing machines running in time t(n) and space s(n) (for example, the "membership/computation" languages whose recognition by a 2DPDA would imply nontrivial simulations of time- or space-bounded Turing machines by 2DPDAs). Each individual L_n is a candidate language whose 2DPDA recognizability is in question, and the family is constructed so that 2DPDA membership of even one L_n would yield a nontrivial complexity-theoretic consequence.

Question: Does there exist at least one index n such that L_n ∈ 2DPDA? Equivalently, given such a family of languages, must the family contain a member that is recognized by some two-way deterministic pushdown automaton?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a classical line of work reducing major open problems in computational complexity (deterministic vs. nondeterministic, time vs. space) to questions about membership of specific language families in 2DPDA. Subsequent literature (e.g., Aho–Hopcroft–Ullman-style simulations, and later revisitations of two-way pushdown simulation) has refined simulation bounds but has not, as far as the available sources indicate, settled whether such constructed families always contain a 2DPDA member. No definitive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in the theory of computation as questions about two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces open problems in complexity theory to questions about 2DPDA languages.
status_evidence.claim: The original framework formulates the question as an open problem about families of languages and 2DPDA membership.

status_evidence.title: Simulation of Two-Way Pushdown Automata Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Revisits simulation bounds for two-way pushdown automata.
status_evidence.claim: Later work refines simulation results but does not resolve the family-membership questions.
